Use case: stylized-concept. Create an entirely new Consecrated Ground painting. Image 1 is a STYLE and LIGHT-HIERARCHY reference only, not a scene to copy. A worn roadside sanctuary open to the evening air: a low cracked imperial stone altar bearing a very weathered sun relief, grasses at the paving joints, a single small clay oil lamp. One tired ordinary male traveller, small at the side of the composition, has just entered and lowers his pack, his face barely resolved in shadow. The sanctuary and its warm patch of ground are the focus; no heroic portrait, no smiling group, no circle of people. Medium-wide composition, generous quiet stone and air, a concentrated amber light against restrained cool shadows. Give the old stone an affecting presence through shape, light and selective painted wear. No magic dome, rays from heaven or dense flowers. The reference supplies economical brushwork and organizing light, not its lion, healer or detailed layout.

Her existing arm anatomy and static stance are rejected. REBUILD the figure and adjust the viewpoint to make the requested anatomy unmistakable.

Show her USING FROST TO CROSS THE CANAL. Recompose into a clear three-quarter FRONT view of her whole body, face and chest visible, her gaze turned down toward image-left. Her anatomical RIGHT shoulder and arm are on the LEFT side of the image, extending comfortably outward and slightly downward toward image-left to cast frost, palm down. Her anatomical LEFT shoulder and arm are on the RIGHT side of the image, lowered naturally beside her body, that left hand carrying the single small amber lantern by its top handle. The arms have separate uninterrupted silhouettes, attach to opposite sides of the ribcage, and do not cross. Push the cloak back from the upper arms enough to see those connections. Exactly two arms total: right hand casting, left hand carrying. No arm at the belt, no third hand, no lantern attached to her belt. Relaxed, ordinary five-fingered hands.

She is taking a careful, purposeful step FROM a low stone water landing ONTO ice she has just made. Her anatomical right boot, at image-left, is planted on a broad solid pale-blue ice shelf on the canal surface; the left foot is still behind on the low stone step at image-right. Give this a modest easy step, not a lunge or leap; the landing is only one shallow step above the water. Show the two legs coherently emerging from her hips, no crossing, with the skirt/coat parted enough to read her stance. Her leading sole sits visibly on opaque supportive ice, not on liquid water or a mere line of frost. Fine branching rime and a little cold vapour spread from under the casting palm into a narrow walkable ice path ahead toward the left foreground. Dark open water beside it establishes that she is freezing a route, not attacking anyone.

Keep familiar canal stonework, a modest moored boat and a quiet distant arcade with a few warm windows as subordinated setting, all in consistent human scale and perspective. Adjust their arrangement to support this front-facing pose; do not preserve the old side-view staging at the expense of anatomy.

Traditional painted fantasy, measured visible brushwork, matte skin, cloth and stone. Selective sharp accents around her hands, the amber lantern and the boot meeting ice; quieter background and secondary edges remain legible without camera blur. Face natural and simply observed, no waxy cheeks, glamour retouching or tiny perfect nose. No uniformly fine surface detail, 3D animation appearance, giant spell blast, text, card frame or signature.
changes.inspection_note: Inspected the complete figure: right shoulder on image-left connects through elbow and wrist to the casting hand; opposite left shoulder connects to the lowered lantern hand at image-right. Two arms total. Two coherent legs, with leading right boot supported by ice and left boot on the low stone step. Lantern hangs from the left hand, clear of the legs. Blue/cold water and amber light retained. Awaiting creator review.
changes.brief: The dark-haired female Gnosis mage uses Frost to cross a winter canal. A three-quarter front view makes the anatomy clear: her anatomical right arm, at image-left, casts toward a newly freezing path; her anatomical left arm, at image-right, hangs naturally with the amber lantern held by its handle. Her leading right boot rests on a solid ice shelf while her left foot remains on a low stone step. Two connected arms and two coherent legs, a clear boot-to-ice contact and ordinary human scale take priority. Retain the blue cloak, warm lantern against cold water, moored boat and quietly painted arcade. This replaces the rejected side-on stance and duplicated-right-arm presentation.
